strings.old: AI video editing works best when it is organized like a post-production team: each specialist has one craft, and all of them share one brief. Kaviyan is built that way. Five AI agents (Cut, Hue, Nova, Echo and Flow) work inside the editing software you already use, on your own timeline. This guide explains what each agent does, how to brief them, and where a human editor should still make the call.
strings.new: A migrated site is a folder of plain files you can host anywhere. Some clients want more: a real codebase in the framework their developers use. Port, Aethron's framework agent, writes that app for you. This guide explains what Port carries, what it rewrites, and how Aethron decides a port is good enough to hand over.

strings.new: What a port carries, and what it rewrites

strings.old: An AI video editor is strongest at the first pass and the repeated pass: assembling selects, matching shots, cleaning audio, resizing for another format. It does not decide what the story is. In Kaviyan every cut, grade and effect the agents make stays fully editable, so the editor keeps the final word on each one.
strings.new: Port does not redraw your design. It reads each page the way a browser renders it, keeps the layout, type and colours exactly, and writes them into the framework you pick. Only the platform's own code is left behind, so the app has no link back to Framer or Webflow.

strings.old: The five agents and their crafts
Cut builds the rough cut from your footage, trims dead air and tightens the pacing, shot by shot. Give it the running time and the order of ideas. It returns an assembly you can rearrange.
strings.new: Astro is the target we have measured most: on the Agero template the port matched the original text 100%, with all 26 headings and every image.

strings.old: Hue balances exposure, matches shots from different cameras and applies the grade. Point it at a reference frame or a saved look, and it carries that look across the whole timeline.
strings.new: Next.js and React produce a normal project your developer can run. They are graded the same way, and refused when they drift.

strings.old: Each market needs its own titles, prices, currency and legal lines. Each channel needs its own aspect ratio. In past seasons Maison Vire’s editors duplicated the master project for every market, replaced the text by hand and exported each version three times. Feedback arrived by email, often about the wrong file.
strings.new: A template stores the same text in more than one place: the page, the code that redraws it, and sometimes a content file. Change one and miss another, and the page quietly puts the old text back when it loads. A file check alone cannot see it.

strings.old: Sara Lindqvist, Creative Director at Maison Vire, counted the cost after the spring campaign: eleven weeks from locked edit to the last regional delivery. By then the collection had been in stores for a month.
strings.new: We met this on real sites: a marquee line with an extra space, a heading split into one span per letter, an image used in seven sizes.

strings.old: For the autumn campaign the team changed the order of work.
